title: CP2463-23 Devon & Torbay Local Electric Vehicle Infrastructure
description:
Concession contract for:\r
\r
The Councils intend to work with Private Sector Partner(s) (PSP) using a concessions approach, supplemented with the LEVI Capital Funding, to deliver approximately 2000 electric vehicle chargepoints in car parks and on-street locations across Devon & Torbay.\r
\r
This is a joint project between Devon County Council and Torbay Council. The Devon District authorities (East Devon District Council, Exeter City Council, Mid Devon District Council, Teignbridge District Council, South Hams District Council, Torridge District Council, and West Devon Borough Council) and Devon Parish Councils are also delivery partners contributing to the successful delivery of the project, which will include granting leases at council owned car parks.\r
\r
The Lots for this procurement are split based on the type of chargepoint, as per the Specification. \r
\r
Lot 1 is for Rapids DC (50kW+)\r
Lot 2 is for Fast AC (22kW)\r
Lot 3 is for Standard AC (<8kW) Bollard Chargepoints\r
Lot 4 is for On-Street Lamp Column Chargepoints \r
\r
Although at the outset Torbay Council will not be awarded under every Lot, the Authority reserves the right to modify the contract to allow Torbay Council to call off at a later date by mutual agreement with the successful provider.

title: ED0234-22 East Devon Tourism Network
description:
NOTE RESERVED CONTRACT

This contract is reserved for suppliers based in the county of Devon. 

East Devon District Council (EDDC) adopted a new Tourism Strategy for East Devon in September 2022, which seeks to support the tourism sector to achieve sustainable growth and deliver economic benefits to the district.  

One of the objectives of the strategy is to build a sustainable, collaborative, private sector network, which will
foster collaboration based on the shared values of quality, net zero, and improved accessibility.  

East Devon District Council is now seeking to commission a third party (the network partner) to develop, manage and support a network of local businesses which has the following characteristics: 

· The network must cover the entire geography of East Devon 
· The network will be built on engagement with predominantly the private sector  
· The network will have access to a public-facing website hosting a comprehensive 'What's On' listing of visitor-focused cultural 
   and tourism events 
· The network will be committed to the values of quality, Net Zero, improving accessibility and collaboration.

title: ED0308-24 Brief for the development of a Tree Strategy
description:
The purpose of the Tree Strategy for East Devon DC will be to ensure there is both continuity and synergy with the Devon Tree & Woodland Strategy 2024. The Devon Strategy provides the county-wide framework for how we can look to increase our tree and woodland cover as well as linking with Local Nature Recovery work, Climate Change adaptation and mitigation targets and also how we engage all our partners, communities and organisations in helping to ensure we manage our treescapes and woodlands. 
An ambition of this Tree Strategy will be to look to set an achievable target for planting trees over the ten year period of the plan which links directly to our Climate Change Strategy and also with the planned Local Nature Recovery Plan for East Devon. 
In doing so we will aim to increase the number of trees unavoidably lost with the caveat of the unknown quantity of trees which may be lost to ash dieback.
The trees that are planted will see the district's tree canopy cover significantly increase by the time they are fully grown. 
We will look to adopt the principle of "the right tree for the right place" in order to ensure the most resilient tree population possible.
We will look to undertake a canopy survey of the trees within East Devon's towns so that we can better understand our tree cover. The canopy survey, including our existing TPO database, council owned tree inventory (Ezytreev) and tree planting initiatives across East Devon (EDDC, developers* etc) should be available for our residents to access on the Council's website.
We will work constructively with Town & Parish Councils, communities and environmental groups to deliver these ambitions and capture this sentiment within the` Vision statement' for the Strategy

title: ED0316-24 Exmouth Seawall Phase 2 - Sheet Pile Wall
description:
Contract documents available from 2nd September. Works to be complete by end of February 2025. Works to start on site ASAP to make use of better working conditions. 



Phase 1 completed in July 2024 . Phase 2 target start date 7th October 2024. Works involved installation of 150m linear length Anchored sheet pile wall with deviation around concession buildings. Sheet pile lengths between 9.5-10 metres. Rock anchors on every In-pan length of anchors 18m.

Phase 2 is 3 types of pile design, for the remaining length of wall around 2 standing concessions, and one area where the concession has been removed. They will tie into Phase 1 works to the East, and a slipway to the west.  The area will need to be made good post works, and handrailing installed.  A set of steps is also proposed.   We are proposing Tied, cantilever and anchored designs, all using the same pile section (of which 43 piles are to be supplied by the client (on site))

title: ED0361-25 - LAD 1 Completion - Heating & Fabric Upgrades
description:
The properties included in LAD 1 project were generally semi-detached and mid-terrace bungalows, some houses were also included.
All properties included are of traditional masonry construction (cavity walls) wither face brick or painted render finish with duo pitch roofs with either a tile or natural/artificial slate roof covering.
All the properties were on either electric Economy 7 or solid fuel heating/hot water.
The work required varies from property to property generally comprising of the following:
•
Heating upgrades (ASHP or high-performance storage heaters i.e. Dimplex Quantum).
•
Solar PV.
•
External wall insulation e.g. cavity wall insulation (Thermabead) or external wall insulation.
•
Roof/loft space insulation (generally top up of existing).
•
Replacement windows/external doors.
•
Draught proofing.
As part of the work, some properties may require:
•
Re-roofing.
•
Strengthening of the roof structure prior to installing solar PV.
•
External decoration including remedial rendering work.
As part of this project, we also recommend the following additional work, costs would come from a separate budget:
•
Upgrading the fire detection/alarm to Grade D Category LD1 standard in accordance with BS 5839-6.
•
Installation of Environmental sensors (AICO Homelink + hub) to monitor for damp & mould, support Disrepair Claim responses.

title: CP2334-22 Recycling of District Council's Glass Bottles and Jars
description:
As a Waste Disposal Authority (WDA) DCC is responsible for the disposal of waste that the District Councils of Devon collect, known as Local Authority Collected Waste (LACW). DCC works in partnership with all 8 District Councils in Devon as well as the unitary authorities (UA) of Torbay. The partnership, known as DASWC (The Devon Authorities Strategic Waste Committee), consists of representatives at both officer and councillor level from all Devon District Councils and Torbay Council.\r
\r
From 1st April 2024, Waste Glass from Exeter City Council and the District Councils of East Devon, Mid-Devon, North Devon and Teignbridge will require collection and haulage from their respective Waste Collection Points for Recovery at the Contractor's Waste Recovery Point(s). The Waste Collection Point locations are listed within the specification provided in the contract documents, along with the estimated annual tonnage. Appendix A within the procurement documents provides further detail regarding each Waste Collection Point.\r
\r
The estimated value of this contract as stated within this contract notice is based off only the historic haulage costs payable to the winning contractor. However there are a number of additional elements to the value of the contract that are tied to the published letsrecycle.com rates, due to the variable nature of this value it is not possible to provide expected values for this element of the contract. Any prospective bidder should ensure they have fully read and understood all elements of the specification in order to accurately determine its value.\r
\r
The Contract will be for an initial period of three years with option to extend for a further two years

noticeIdentifier: Design and Build of a Multi-Use Games Area (MUGA), Cranbrook (East Devon)
title: Design and Build of a Multi-Use Games Area (MUGA), Cranbrook (East Devon)
description:
Cranbrook in East Devon is a town which is being developed on a former green field site from scratch. Construction works started in 2011 and the first residents moved in during the following year. By early 2024, the town had grown to approximately 9,000 residents occupying just under 3,500 properties. The current Local Plan which covers the period until 2031 makes provision for the delivery of circa 8,000 homes housing in the region of 25,000 residents - so Cranbrook will be at least a medium-sized town and probably the second-biggest settlement in East Devon. 

As part of the development, multi-use sports pitches were delivered in 2019 which are well-used. Cranbrook Town Council manages the sports pitches and is now looking to commission the construction of a multi-use games area (MUGA) at the site. This opportunity sets out the parameters and the Town Council is now inviting tenders for the design and construction works to enable the above.

title: CP2300-22 - Contract for the Treatment of Organic Sweepings Waste
description:
Devon County Councils current contract arrangements for the transportation and treatment of Organic Sweepings Waste collected by the eight district councils within Devon is due to expire at the end of March 2024 and as such DCC are seeking to reprocure this service.  It is intended that the new contract will operate from 1st April 2024 for an initial period of five years with the option to extend the contract by a period or periods totalling a maximum further 5 years.\r
\r
Organic Sweepings Waste mainly consists of organic matter and as such DCC wishes the waste to be treated to allow it to be recycled e.g. into a compost like product or similar.\r
\r
The service requirement has been divided into two lots and DCC intends to let a contract for each lot.   Bidders can submit bids for one or both lots with no limit on the number of lots to be awarded to one provider.  Bids for each lot must be independent and not reliant on being awarded both lots.\r
\r
The Lots are as follows\r
\r
Service Lot 1 Contract for the transportation and Treatment of Organic Sweepings Waste from the District Councils of \r
East Devon\r
Exeter\r
Mid Devon\r
North Devon\r
South Hams\r
Torridge\r
West Devon\r
\r
Organic Sweepings waste arising from the District Councils covered in Lot 1 will require transportation from Waste Collection Points provided by DCC or District Council to the Contractors Waste Treatment Point for Treatment.\r
\r
During the 2022 23 Financial Year approximately 3600 tonnes of Organic Sweepings were collected as part of the District Councils covered by Lot 1 sweeping operations. \r
\r
Service Lot 2 Contract for the transportation and Treatment of Organic Sweepings Waste from Teignbridge District Council.\r
\r
The Contractor is required provide their own Waste Reception Point within the administrative boundary of Teignbridge District Council to which Organic Sweepings Waste can be delivered by Teignbridge District Council.   After Teignbridge District Council has delivered their Organic Sweepings Waste to the Contractors Waste Reception Point the Contractor shall transport the waste to the Contractors Waste Treatment Point for Treatment.\r
\r
During the 2022 23 Financial Year Teignbridge District Council collected approximately 950 tonnes of Organic Sweepings as part of their sweeping operations.\r
\r

Cranbrook in East Devon started being constructed in 2011 on land which used to be green fields. By early 2024, approximately 9,000 residents occupied 3,200 or so dwellings; this figure is projected to rise to approximately 25,000 residents occupying 8,000 homes.
Cranbrook Town Council is now looking to appoint a supplier for the design and build of a trim trail in the Stone Meadow area of the Country Park in Cranbrook as set out in this opportunity in order to further enhance the amenities and facilities which are available for the benefit of local residents and visitors.
Any prospective supplier is invited to submit their design proposal(s) in accordance with the specification set out in this opportunity to the Town Council.

title: CP2523-24 Mid Devon Shared Prosperity Fund Support Provision for Businesses
description: Devon County Council (DCC) is currently running a business support programme funded by UK Shared Prosperity Fund (SPF) until March 2025 called Prosper. Prosper offers a range of support to businesses and start-ups in Mid Devon, East Devon, and Exeter. Support is delivered through a mixture of in-person and online support, on a 1-2-1 or workshop basis. Prosper support is split into four Lots: General business support, Green business support, Entrepreneur support, & Job creation and safeguarding support. These lots support DCC and it's local authority partners to meet the aims of SPF and achieve specific SPF outputs and outcomes. However, business demand has changed in Mid Devon and it's necessary to procure more general and start up support here instead of jobs created.

title: Scaffolding Framework 2024
description:
Westward Housing Group (WHG) wish to appoint contractors to provide services across our stock portfolio. Contractors will be required to provide advice, quotations and scaffolding erection and removal to WHG properties as and when required. 

The tender is divided into five Lots by geographical area:

Lot 1	West Cornwall to Bodmin		(all TR postcodes)

Lot 2	Mid & East Cornwall and Plymouth	(all PL postcodes)

Lot 3	South Devon				(all TQ postcodes)

Lot 4	East Devon and Taunton		(EX1-17 & EX24)

Lot 5	North Devon				(EX18-23 & EX31-39)

 
You may bid for any number of lots.
You must be able to service the entire area of your chosen Lot(s).
In the pricing document is a tab for you to indicate which Lots you are applying for.


The Framework

The tender will generate a maximum of three contractors for each geographical area. It will be at the procuring officers' discretion to apportion the works based on value for money, previous performance with the framework and availability of contractor to complete the works. 
A mini competition may be undertaken, where the requirement is of a more complex nature, or the value is estimated to be in excess of £30,000.
Westward Housing Group withholds the right to retender the framework or exclude a contractor from the framework should they choose to legally do so.

noticeIdentifier: Delivery of a Wheeled Sports Facility in Cranbrook, Devon
title: Delivery of a Wheeled Sports Facility in Cranrbook, Devon
description:
A consortium of developers, the East Devon New Community Partners, is delivering the currently consented first 3,500 homes at Cranbrook in East Devon. The Section 106 agreement relating to this development secures the preparation and servicing of land for a "Skateboard Park" prior to 2,250 dwelling occupations. The responsibility for the delivery of the skatepark transferred to the Town Council earlier in 2021. Cranbrook Town Council is now looking to appoint a preferred supplier for the construction of a wheeled sports facility in a town centre location in Cranbrook as set out in the tender documents.

Any prospective supplier is invited to submit their design proposal(s) in accordance with the specification set out in the tender documents to the Town Council.

noticeIdentifier: Cranbrook Ingrams Sports Pavilion - Design and Build
title: Cranbrook Ingrams Sports Pavilion - Design and Build
description:
Cranbrook in East Devon is a town which is being developed on a former green field site from scratch. Construction works started in 2011 and the first residents moved in during the following year. By early 2021, the town had grown to approximately 6,000 residents occupying around 2,300 properties. The current Local Plan which covers the period until 2031 makes provision for the delivery of circa 8,000 homes housing in the region of 25,000 residents - so Cranbrook will be at least a medium-sized town and probably the second-biggest settlement in East Devon.

As part of the development, multi-use sports pitches were delivered in 2019 which are well- used, predominantly by youth teams. Cranbrook Town Council manages the sports pitches and is now commissioning the construction of a community sports pavilion at the site. The tender documents set out the parameters and the Town Council is now inviting tenders for the design and construction works to enable the above.

title: NHS Devon - Peer Support Network - Supporting Young People's Neurodiverse Needs
description:
NHS Devon Integrated Care Board sought to commission a Peer Support Network in Torbay.  The focus of this network will be to work alongside the First Steps handbook and will include the current co-produced support guides and skills workshops establish by Parental Minds in East Devon.

The network will be for parents/care givers who are supporting their youngster's mental wellbeing.  Research evidence  shows that early intervention, changes of language and empowering parents/care givers with additional skills can improve the long-term outcomes for these youngsters and is particularly useful for neurodiverse families.  

The contract term is for 1 year commencing 01 March 2023.  The Annual Contract Value is £15,000

title: CP2482-24 DCC Tree Management Framework - Tree Inspection and Tree Surgery
description:
This opportunity is for the establishment of a Framework to provide a number of contractors to provide Tree Surgery and Tree Inspection services across Devon. The tree population is spread widely across Devon and trees are to be found on 650+ occupied properties and alongside up to 12 500 km of DCC highways. This corresponds to an estimate of over 3 000 000 trees across the DCC estate and alongside Highways. The contract is split into a number of Lots and Sub Lots as listed below.\r
\r
- Lot 1a - Scheduled Inspections of Highways - Driven and Walked\r
- Lot 1b - Schedule Inspection of Premises - Walked\r
- Lot 1c - Ad Hoc Inspections of Highways (All Types)\r
- Lot 1d - Ad Hoc Inspections of Non-Highways (All Types)\r
- Lot 2a - Highways Tree Surgery (Non-Emergency)\r
- Lot 2b - Non-Highways Tree Surgery (Non-Emergency)\r
- Lot 2c - Highways Tree Surgery (Emergency)\r
- Lot 2d - Non-Highways Tree Surgery (Emergency)\r
\r
The framework additionally operates across a geographic split of 9 regions across the County, these regions are set as the eight district council boundaries and Plymouth. Each of the Lots/Sublots above will have a number (Defined within the procurement documentation) of organisations appointed in each of these geographic regions. The specific detailed specification, service requirements and and required staffing and accreditation levels can be found within the procurement documentation pack.\r
\r
The Framework will operate for a period of four years, commencing on the 1st April 2025, the framework will be open for use to all Public Sector authorities, councils and organisations within Devon. An indicative list of public sectors eligible to access this agreement can be found within schedule 3 of the procurement documentation.
